title.narrative: Chad Digitalization of Revenue Administrations and COVID-19 Response Project

description.narrative: The development objectives of Domestic Resource Mobilization and Management Project for Chad is to improve performance, processes, and transparency in key government entities for revenue mobilization. This project has three components. 1) The first component, Results-based Financing to Support Change Management in Customs and Tax administrations, has the flowing subcomponents: (i) Support the utilization of a unified taxpayers registry for enterprises; (ii) Support the gradual adoption of electronic filing by large taxpayers; (iii) Support the roll out of mandatory tax payment by large taxpayers through the banking system; (iv) Support the gradual adoption of pay-by-phone by Small Taxpayers; and(v) Reduction in the number of physical custom inspections of imported merchandise; (vi) Reduction in the release time for imported merchandise. 2) The second component, Technical Assistance to Strengthen Revenue Agencies, aims to provide specialized TA, including technical experts for each area of intervention, to improve transparency, and increase accountability of the tax and customs administrations, petroleum, and telecom for revenue mobilization and management. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Improve Tax Administration and Policy; (ii) Improve Customs Administration; (iii) Increasing Transparency and Accountability of the Recipient's Revenue Agencies; (iv) Address Fiscal Challenges and Improve the Oversight of the ICT Sector; and (v) Improve the Management and Control of Revenue Generation in the Petroleum. 3) The third component, Project Management and Coordination, aims to support the ST-PAMFIP—a dedicated Project Implementation Unit embedded in the MoFB—to undertake project management, in accordance with the World Bank's fiduciary and other guidelines, including incremental operating costs, equipment, training on fiduciary and project management issues, project audits, and engagement of technical experts to provide technical expertise on project performance monitoring and planning.
To improve performance, processes, and transparency in key government entities for revenue mobilization.

title.narrative: Share of imported merchandise subject to physical inspections

baseline.value: 100 percent of imported merchandise is subject to physical inspections.

target.value: No more than 80 percent of imported merchandise is subject to physical inspections

comment.narrative: <p>The connection of existing scanners to ASYCUDA World is scheduled in February 2023. The team will monitor the completion of this indicator with UNCTAD and the customs administration.</p>

actual.value: 100 percent of imported merchandise is subject to physical inspections

title.narrative: Share of large taxpayers paying through the banking system

baseline.value: 20 percent of large taxpayers use the banking system

target.value: At least 70 percent of large taxpayers pay through the banking system.

comment.narrative: <p>PDO#5 (DLI#6). The restructuring upgraded this DLI as PDO to better refelct project's outcome. This PDO is achieved.</p >

actual.value: 100 percent of large taxpayers pay through the banking system.

title.narrative: Establishment of unique identification number for enterprises for all administrations

baseline.value: Multiple taxpayers identification number are used across the administration

target.value: Multiple taxpayers identification numbers are still used across the administration.

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator is not met. The launch of the registration module of e-tax is effective since January 2023. However, the upd ate of the taxpayer's database, is still in progress.</p>

actual.value: The regulation defining the responsibility for the establishment and management of the unified taxpayers registry and the procedure for registration is adopted

title.narrative: Number of customs offices in which ASYCUDA World has been rolled out

comment.narrative:
<p>The migration to ASYCUDA World is completed in 36 customs offices, above the final target of 4 customs offices. The deploym ent is effective in the following customs offices: Ngueli (6) Aeroport, Adji Kosei, Colis Postaux, Koutere (2) Moundou (2), At i, Daboua, Bol, Bagasola, Mao, Abeche, Goz-Beida, Adre (2), Bongor, Kome, Kelo, Ronier, Lere (2), Doba, Gueleding, Sahr, Djerm aya, Cimaf, Fianga, Pala, Koumra.</p>
<p>???????During the ICR mission, the government shared data for 45 customs offices.</p>

title.narrative: Share of small entities paying Presumptive Income Tax for Small Entities (Impt gnrale libratoire) by mobile payment

baseline.value: 0 percent of small taxpayers pay by mobile payment

target.value: 10 percent of small taxpayers pay by mobile payment

comment.narrative: <p>The E-tax system, including the mobile payment system was launched in January 2023. 6,838 small taxpayers have represent 18.69 percent of the total number of taxpayers (36,737) as per data collected during TADAT.</p>

actual.value: 18.69 percent of small taxpayers pay by mobile payment

title.narrative: Average time for imported goods to clear customs at targeted customs offices

comment.narrative: <p>PDO#2 (DLI#7) : The restructuring linked this PDO indicator to a newly introduced DLI, to accelerate the achievement of the final target (12 hours) by June 30, 2023. Its targeting was also revised to target the offices where ASYCUDA World will be de ployed. Reduction of customs clearance time exceeds target in selected offices (Ngueli, Koutere, Adji Kossei)</p>

title.narrative: DLI#2: Share of food, necessity items and sanitary products imported to fight the COVID-19 pandemic, as identified in Circular 04/PR/MFB/2020, cleared through customs in less than 72 hours.

comment.narrative:
<p>PBC 2 is fully achieved and disbursed. The end target of 60% at December 31, 2020 was
exceeded. 98% of food, necessity item s and sanitary products imported to fight the COVID-19 pandemic
are cleared in less than 72 hours.</p>

title.narrative: Share of approved VAT refunds claims paid through the new mechanism

baseline.value: No payment has been processed through the new mechanism

target.value: At least 15 percent of approved VAT refunds claims are paid through the new mechanism

comment.narrative: <p>PDO#6 (DLI#8). The restructuring introduced a new indicator, the refund of VAT credits through the new refund mechanism imp lemented in March 2022 (PDO#6). A payment order of 102 million representing 15.79% of approved VAT claims have been issued on June 09 to refund the VAT to the concerned taxpayers. The PDO will be achieved after the processing of those orders by t he central bank.</p>

actual.value: Five VAT refund claims were issued, which represents 15.79 percent of the approved claims

title.narrative: Publication of annual reports on tax expenditures

comment.narrative: <p>For PDO#7 (DLI#9). This PDO is achieved, The reports are published on the Ministry of Finance and OTFip websites. Tec hnical assistance will be mobilized through the Bank executed trust fund to strengthen the tax administration capacity to asse ss and analyze tax expenditures in line with international best practices.</p>

actual.value: Two annual reports on tax expenditures are published
